Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a common fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis that damages foliage, blossoms, and fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves; leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely; scabby lesions on fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or captan/myclobutanil at green tip through petal fall. Prune diseased twigs.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Ensure good tree canopy airflow through selective pruning.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, causing frog-eye leaf spots and fruit rot.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots enlarging into concentric rings with dark margins; fruit develops firm black mummified rot.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out dead wood, fire blight cankers, and mummified apples. Apply thiophanate-methyl or captan.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitize pruning tools between cuts. Avoid wounding fruit during handling.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae is a heteroecious fungus requiring junipers and apple trees to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow circular spots on upper leaf surfaces; tube-like aecia structures on leaf undersides.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Spray myclobutanil, tebuconazole, or mancozeb at pink bud stage through petal fall.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove eastern red cedar trees within a 1-mile radius of apple orchards where practical; plant rust-resistant cultivars.

Apple___healthy.description: Apple foliage shows vigorous chlorophyll activity with no pathological pathogen presence.
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Uniformly green, firm leaves with no lesion, chlorosis, or necrotic margins.
Apple___healthy.treatment: No fungicide application needed. Maintain regular balanced N-P-K nutrition and seasonal irrigation.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Regular scouting every 7-10 days; maintain dormant oil spray for insect vector suppression.

Blueberry___healthy.description: Blueberry canopy exhibits optimal vegetative growth in acidic soil conditions.
Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Smooth green foliage, upright canes, and healthy photosynthetic vigor.
Blueberry___healthy.treatment: No disease treatment required. Maintain soil pH between 4.5 and 5.2 with elemental sulfur if needed.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Apply pine bark mulch, ensure drip irrigation, and avoid overhead watering.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Caused by Podosphaera clandestina, affecting leaves and succulent shoots, reducing fruit quality.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal mycelium on leaf undersides; leaf curling and distorted terminal growth.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray sulfur-based formulations, potassium bicarbonate, or quinoxyfen at petal fall.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Improve canopy aeration with summer pruning; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Cherry tree leaves and shoots are healthy and free from bacterial canker and mildew.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Intact, green leaves with smooth cuticles and strong internode growth.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.treatment: Maintain routine orchard maintenance and balanced fertilization.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Copper sprays during leaf fall to protect against bacterial canker entries.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Gray leaf spot is caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis, a major foliar disease in warm, humid corn-growing belts.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions restricted by leaf veins; lesions coalesce causing severe premature blighting.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides (azoxystrobin + propiconazole) at silking (R1 stage).
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Crop rotation away from corn for at least 1-2 years; deep tillage of crop residue.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Common rust is caused by the airborne fungus Puccinia sorghi, favored by cool, moist conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, powdery golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Foliar application of pyraclostrobin or tebuconazole when pustules appear before tassel emergence.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids with Rp gene complexes; plant early in the season.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum, capable of causing up to 50% grain yield loss when established before tasseling.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2-15 cm long) on foliage.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Foliar fungicide application (mancozeb, pyraclostrobin, or trifloxystrobin) at first sign of lower leaf lesions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids with Ht genes; rotate with non-host crops like soybean or sunflower.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Corn plants exhibit optimal leaf area index and green chlorophyll distribution.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Broad, arching green leaves with robust venation and zero fungal pustules or lesions.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment: No pathogen remediation needed. Maintain timely split nitrogen applications.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Monitor for armyworm and stalk borer pest pressure.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Guignardia bidwellii causes destructive rot in grape foliage, young shoots, and ripening berries.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves; berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply myclobutanil or mancozeb starting at 1-inch shoot growth until bunch closure.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune and destroy all mummified berries from the vine and vineyard floor before bud break.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Complex vascular wood decay disease caused by fungi including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Fomitiporia.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe interveinal chlorosis and necrosis on leaves; dark purple speckling on berry skins.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No curative chemical. Paint large pruning wounds with trichoderma or sealants; trunk renewal surgery.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid pruning in wet weather; disinfect pruning shears with 70% ethanol.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Caused by Phaeoisariopsis vitis, a late-season foliar pathogen causing premature vine defoliation.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular brown spots with distinct reddish or dark margins on mature leaves; black spore tufts underneath.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Post-harvest or late summer copper oxychloride or carbendazim sprays.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Canopy management for airflow; gather and compost fallen foliage.

Grape___healthy.description: Grapevine canopy shows balanced vegetative-reproductive vigor.
Grape___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green palmate leaves with clean veins, firm petioles, and healthy berry clusters.
Grape___healthy.treatment: Continue standard fertigation and trellis canopy training.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Scout weekly for powdery mildew and spider mites.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Citrus Greening is caused by the phloem-limited bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, vectored by psyllids.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy yellow mottle on leaves; small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green at the stylar end.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure once infected. Immediate aggressive chemical suppression of Asian citrus psyllid with imidacloprid.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant certified disease-free nursery stock; apply systemic insecticides; remove symptomatic trees promptly.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni causes severe leaf spotting, defoliation, and fruit pitting.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Angular, water-soaked lesions that turn purple-brown and drop out leaving a shot-hole appearance; pitted fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply preventive copper bactericide or oxytetracycline sprays starting at shuck split.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant peach varieties; install windbreaks to minimize blowing sand wounds.

Peach___healthy.description: Peach foliage is thriving with uniform cell turgidity and no bacterial shot-holing.
Peach___healthy.symptoms: Lanceolate, glossy green leaves with no spotting, gumming, or curl.
Peach___healthy.treatment: Maintain seasonal irrigation and micronutrient zinc/boron foliar sprays.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Apply dormant copper spray before bud swell to control peach leaf curl.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas euvesicatoria, a seed-borne and splash-dispersed bacterial pathogen.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, circular, water-soaked dark spots on leaves with yellow halos; leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray fixed copper mixed with mancozeb, or actigard systemic acquired resistance inducer.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified hot-water treated seeds; drip irrigate instead of overhead sprinklers.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Bell pepper plants have dense, dark green foliage and strong stem architecture.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Evenly pigmented green leaves with no marginal scorch or water-soaked lesions.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.treatment: Regular balanced fertigation with calcium-rich inputs to prevent blossom end rot.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Scout for whiteflies and aphids; mulch rows with organic straw.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Alternaria solani causes early blight in solanaceous crops, reducing tuber bulking capacity.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions with concentric rings (target-board pattern) on older lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or difenoconazole upon first appearance of lower leaf lesions.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Ensure adequate nitrogen nutrition (stressed plants are more susceptible); rotate with legumes or grains.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Phytophthora infestans is an oomycete responsible for devastating late blight and crop failure.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green lesions turning dark brown/black; white velvety fungal mold on underside during humid mornings.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Immediate systemic fungicide spray: Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb, Cymoxanil, or Dimethomorph.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles; plant certified disease-free seed tubers.

Potato___healthy.description: Potato crop exhibits healthy vegetative growth and active photosynthesis.
Potato___healthy.symptoms: Compound leaves are firm, vibrant green, and free from chlorosis and blights.
Potato___healthy.treatment: Support tuber initiation with potassium-heavy fertigation.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain protective ridging to protect underground tubers from spore wash.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Raspberry canes demonstrate healthy primocane and floricane development.
Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Compound serrated leaves are vivid green, lacking spur blight or cane botrytis.
Raspberry___healthy.treatment: Maintain trellis support and consistent soil moisture.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune out spent floricanes immediately after fruiting.

Soybean___healthy.description: Soybean canopy has active nodulation and healthy trifoliate leaves.
Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves have uniform emerald color without rust pustules or sudden death chlorosis.
Soybean___healthy.treatment: Maintain weed control and phosphorus availability for optimal nitrogen fixation.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Inoculate seed with Bradyrhizobium japonicum before planting.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Podosphaera xanthii causes widespread superficial powdery growth on cucurbit leaves and stems.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum-powder-like white spots that expand to cover entire leaf surfaces; leaves yellow and wither.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray neem oil, potassium silicate, or systemic myclobutanil/triflumizole.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Space plants adequately for airflow; choose powdery mildew tolerant squash varieties.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Diplocarpon earlianum causes leaf scorch, reducing crown vigor and berry size.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small, purplish round spots that enlarge; centers turn dark brown and look scorched or burned.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Apply captan, thiram, or azoxystrobin before bloom and after harvest renovation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Renovate strawberry beds after harvest by mowing and removing old diseased leaves.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Strawberry crowns display robust trifoliate leaves and healthy stolons.
Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Glossy, deeply green serrated leaves with no leaf spot or scorch necrosis.
Strawberry___healthy.treatment: Maintain drip irrigation and plastic or straw bed mulching.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Avoid overhead watering; manage spider mite populations.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Xanthomonas spp. cause bacterial spot affecting leaves, stems, and tomato fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark water-soaked spots with yellow halos; leaves take on a ragged, greasy appearance.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray fixed copper compounds combined with mancozeb to overcome copper tolerance.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid working in wet fields; use pathogen-free seed and drip irrigation exclusively.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Alternaria linariae (solani) is a prevalent fungal disease affecting tomato foliage and stems.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric ring target lesions on older lower foliage; collar rot on seedling stems.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Foliar sprays of chlorothalonil, azoxystrobin, or copper hydroxide every 7-10 days.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Stake plants upright; strip lower 12 inches of foliage to prevent soil splash.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Phytophthora infestans is an aggressive oomycete pathogen capable of killing tomato crops within days.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Greasy, water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems; white mold sporulation on leaf undersides in high humidity; firm brown fruit rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Immediate systemic fungicide application: Cymoxanil, Mandipropamid, or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Space rows for maximum air movement; destroy infected debris; avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Passalora fulva causes leaf mold primarily in protected greenhouse and high-humidity cultivation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces; velvety olive-brown spore patches on undersides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply copper fungicides, difenoconazole, or cyazofamid.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce greenhouse relative humidity below 85% with horizontal airflow fans and venting.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria lycopersici is a destructive foliar fungus that causes severe lower-to-upper defoliation.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1-3 mm) with dark brown margins and gray or tan centers containing tiny black pycnidia specks.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Spray mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or copper fungicides at the first sign of lower leaf speckling.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch around tomato stems; implement 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous plants.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tetranychus urticae is a microscopic sap-feeding arachnid pest that explodes in hot, dry conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow/white stippling on leaf surfaces; bronzed, dry leaves; delicate silken webbing between leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray insecticidal soap, neem oil, abamectin, or bifenazate; release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization; overhead wash plants occasionally to raise humidity and dislodge mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Corynespora cassiicola causes target spot on foliage and fruit in warm, humid regions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Pinpoint spots expanding into brown lesions with light brown centers and faint concentric rings without yellow halos.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Improve canopy airflow, avoid excess leaf wetness, and remove infected crop residues.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: TYLCV is a devastating begomovirus transmitted exclusively by the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaflets; stunted growth; chlorotic leaf margins; flower drop with no fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No curative chemical. Manage whitefly vectors aggressively with acetamiprid, spiromesifen, or yellow sticky traps.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use 50-mesh insect-proof netting in nurseries; grow TYLCV-resistant hybrids.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: ToMV is a highly contagious mechanical tobamovirus that spreads via worker hands, tools, and seeds.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves; blistering; shoestring-like narrow leaves; internal fruit browning.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No chemical cure. Rogue and destroy infected plants immediately.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Wash hands and disinfect tools in 20% non-fat dry milk solution; purchase certified virus-free seeds.

Tomato___healthy.description: Tomato plant shows healthy vegetative vigor, clean foliage, and active floral development.
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Rich dark green pinnate leaves, sturdy stems with healthy glandular trichomes, and zero lesions.
Tomato___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Continue regular balanced N-P-K-Ca-Mg fertigation.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain weekly scouting; ensure consistent watering to prevent calcium deficiency blossom end rot.
